title: The Only Points of Interest That Actually Matter For Trading
description: Learn the only three points of interest that matter in trading. Discover when to use Fair Value Gaps, swing highs and lows, and CISD to identify the correct point of interest.

body.text: Introduction
One of the biggest mistakes traders make is using too many points of interest or applying them incorrectly. This often leads to getting stopped out before price reaches the correct point of interest.

The reality is that you don’t need dozens of different concepts to identify where price is likely to react. Instead, you need to understand which points of interest matter and, more importantly, when to use each one.
In this blog, we’ll cover the only three points of interest that matter, the order to use them in, and how to identify the correct point of interest before looking for continuation opportunities.
Every Continuation Starts With a Point of Reversal
Every continuation starts with a point of reversal.
Once that point of reversal has formed, it becomes the protected swing. From there, work from the protected swing toward the current range and ask one simple question:
“Do I have a point of interest?”
If the answer is yes, that becomes the area to begin looking for confirmation.
If the answer is no, continue through the framework until you find the correct point of interest.
The goal isn’t to mark every possible level on your chart. The goal is to identify the correct point of interest before looking for opportunities.
Fair Value Gaps Come First
The first point of interest to look for is a Fair Value Gap.
If a Fair Value Gap exists between the protected swing and the current range, it becomes the point of interest.
There’s no need to continue searching for another level.
A Fair Value Gap always takes priority because it’s the first point of interest within the framework.
Once price reaches that Fair Value Gap, you can begin waiting for confirmation before looking for continuation opportunities.
If There Isn’t a Fair Value Gap, Look for Swing Highs or Lows
If there isn’t a Fair Value Gap, the next point of interest becomes a swing high or swing low.
Again, start at the protected swing and work toward the current range.
If the first point of interest you encounter is a swing high or swing low, that’s the area to monitor.
There’s no need to overcomplicate the analysis.
Simply work through the framework until you identify the first available point of interest.
CISD Is the Final Point of Interest
If there isn’t a Fair Value Gap or a swing high or swing low, the final point of interest becomes a change in state of delivery (CISD).
A CISD isn’t the first place to start.
Instead, it’s the final layer within the framework.
If the first two points of interest aren’t available, a CISD retest becomes the correct point of interest to monitor for confirmation.
Following the same order every time removes unnecessary decision-making and keeps your analysis consistent.
Repeat the Same Process
As new protected swings form, repeat the exact same process.
Start at the protected swing.
Work toward the current range.
Look for a Fair Value Gap.
If one isn’t present, move to a swing high or swing low.
If neither is present, look for a CISD.
Nothing changes.
Every new protected swing follows the same framework.
Adjust as the Market Develops
Markets won’t always trend cleanly.
During consolidations, price may continue creating new protected swings while remaining inside the same range.
As new protected swings develop, your point of interest should adjust with them.
Rather than staying fixed on an older level, continue applying the same framework to the newest protected swing.
Doing this keeps your point of interest relevant to the current market conditions.
A Point of Interest Doesn’t Mean an Entry
Finding the correct point of interest doesn’t mean it’s time to enter a trade.
The point of interest simply tells you where to begin paying attention.
Once price reaches that area, you can begin looking for confirmation before considering an opportunity.
Keeping confirmation separate from the point of interest helps avoid entering too early and allows price to complete its delivery before looking for continuation.
Final Thoughts
The key isn’t finding more points of interest. It’s identifying the correct point of interest by following a consistent framework.
Start with the protected swing.
Work toward the current range.
Look for a Fair Value Gap first.
If there isn’t one, move to a swing high or swing low.
If neither exists, look for a CISD.
Following the same process every time removes unnecessary complexity and helps you identify the correct point of interest before looking for continuation opportunities.
The simpler your framework becomes, the easier it is to stay consistent.
